text_blocks.snippet: Law enforcement and the Better Business Bureau (BBB) in Central Illinois report a high volume of active imposter and AI-driven phone scams.
Current Active Scams in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Law Enforcement & Jury Duty Imposter Calls: Scammers spoof local sheriff's department numbers or use real names of deputies and federal prosecutors, claiming you missed jury duty or have an active arrest warrant . They demand immediate payment via Bitcoin kiosks, cryptocurrency, or gift cards to avoid jail.
Fake Jail/Bond Releases: Fraudsters call family members claiming a loved one is in custody and can be released immediately for a cash or crypto payment.
"Toll Text" Phishing: Fraudulent text messages mimicking the Illinois Tollway claim recipients owe unpaid tolls, directing them to malicious links that steal personal and financial data.

BBB & Utility Imposter Emails/Calls: Scammers send phishing emails or make "verification" calls posing as the Better Business Bureau or utility companies, promising fake reimbursements or threatening immediate shutoffs.
Practice the Pause: Stop and take a breath when a caller creates extreme urgency, demands secrecy, or threatens immediate arrest.
Verify Independently: Hang up and call the official phone number of the agency or business directly rather than using the number provided by the caller.

Know the Rules: Real law enforcement and government offices in Illinois will never call to demand payment over the phone, ask for cryptocurrency/gift cards, or accept bond money over the phone (especially since cash bail ended in the state).
